variety: Bribri of Talamanca, Costa Rica. Headwords follow Krohn's pandialectal dictionary, preferring forms attested in Jara & García Segura (based on Coroma speech, Alí García Segura) and Margery (Amubri/Salitre data); dialect variants (Amubri, Coroma, Salitre) noted per card. Not checked for Panamanian Bribri.
orthography: Bribri practical orthography (Wilson, revised by Constenla; as used by Krohn, UCR and DIPALICORI): nasal vowels marked with a combining macron below (U+0331, the 'underline'), extra vowels ë ö; tone on the stressed syllable: acute = high/rising, grave = falling, circumflex = rising (Amubri); apostrophe = glottal stop; tk is pronounced tch by some speakers (DIPALICORI writes tch). Strings stored NFC. Jara's newer diacritic-only (tilde) nasal spelling is NOT used.

jaguar.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; flores2009 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'jaguar'; primary page not verified)
jaguar.note: Everyday noun for jaguar (Panthera onca). Synonym dulë́kalöm (variants dulë́kalö, dulë́klöm) per Margery 1996/Flores 2009. Variant spelling nmù̱. Sensitivity: the jaguar figures in Bribri narratives and is associated with a clan (Tùbölwak, per Jara & García 2003); the plain animal noun is ordinary vocabulary, but avoid compounds like na̱mù̱ dalë̀ ('jaguar sickness').
jaguar.reviewQuestion: Is na̱mù̱ the word children would use for the jaguar picture, or dulë́kalöm? Which do you prefer for a game?

colibri.source: jaragarcia2003; flores2009; margery1996; dipalicori_animales (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'colibrí'; primary page not verified)
colibri.note: Generic for hummingbirds (Trochilidae); also 'small long-billed bird'. Variants bitsù̱, btsù̱. Many species compounds exist; avoid sibö̀batsu̱ (contains the sacred name Sibö̀).
colibri.reviewQuestion: Is batsù̱ (or bitsù̱/btsù̱) how your community says it?

llama.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
llama.note: No Bribri entry for the Andean llama; the animal is not native to Talamanca. No attested Bribri loan found. Do not substitute another animal.
llama.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

condor.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
condor.note: No Bribri entry for the Andean condor. Related but DIFFERENT birds are attested: ölö́bulu / uchí (king vulture, Sarcoramphus papa), ölö́ (vulture, generic), pú̱ (raptor, generic). Using any of these would name a different animal, so left empty.
condor.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri way to refer to the Andean condor, or would you accept ölö́bulu (king vulture) only if the card art is changed?

mariposa.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; jaragarcia2003; dipalicori_animales (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'mariposa'; primary page not verified)
mariposa.note: Generic for butterflies/moths (Lepidoptera). Variants kuàkua, short form kua’. Blue morpho is dulùkuékua. Also shown in the DIPALICORI animals dictionary as kua’kua / kuâkua.
mariposa.reviewQuestion: Is kua’kua the everyday form, and which tone/spelling do you prefer (kua’kua vs kuàkua)?

guajolote.source: margery1996; rimolo2007 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'chompipe / pavo'; primary page not verified)
guajolote.note: Domestic turkey; Costa Rican Spanish 'chompipe'. Nasal vowel ò̱ (macron below).
guajolote.reviewQuestion: Is chò̱ used for the domestic turkey in your community?

tortuga.source: margery1996; flores2009; dipalicori_animales (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'tortuga'; primary page not verified)
tortuga.note: Generic turtle. Sea turtles have specific names (sö̀ hawksbill, kakò̱ leatherback); freshwater turtle ö̀lëkuë / pó̱kuë. DIPALICORI animals dictionary shows 'sö / ölë kuë' on the turtles page.
tortuga.reviewQuestion: For a generic turtle picture, is kuë̀ right, or would children name a specific kind?

rana.source: margery1996; flores2009; jaragarcia2003; dipalicori_animales (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'rana'; primary page not verified)
rana.note: Generic for frogs and toads. Variants bukë’ (used as the category label in the DIPALICORI animals dictionary) and bkuë’.
rana.reviewQuestion: Which form is used in your variety: bukuë’ or bukë’?

serpiente.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; dipalicori_animales (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'serpiente'; primary page not verified)
serpiente.note: Generic snake. Krohn writes tk for a sound some speakers write tch (DIPALICORI uses tkabë / tchabë). Variant tkbë̀. Ritual-speech synonym tulít — do not use. Note tkabë̀ also means 'rainbow' (see arcoiris), linked to Bribri narratives.
serpiente.reviewQuestion: Should the game spell this tkabë̀ or tchabë̀ for your community?

maiz.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2013 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'maíz'; primary page not verified)
maiz.note: Variants ikuö̀wö / ikuwö̀ (also 'maize grain') and kuwö̀. Many named varieties exist; avoid ritual-speech forms (sékibö etc.).
maiz.reviewQuestion: Is ikuö̀ or ikuö̀wö the better word for a picture of an ear of corn?

nopal.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
nopal.note: No Bribri entry for nopal (Opuntia), which is not a Talamanca plant. The only cactus entry is na̱mù̱yibala (Pereskia grandifolia), a different plant. No attested loan.
nopal.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

frijol.source: margery1996; sanchez_sf (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'frijol'; primary page not verified)
frijol.reviewQuestion: Is átu the usual word for beans?

pina.source: margery1996; sanchez_sf (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'piña'; primary page not verified)
pina.reviewQuestion: Which of abáwö / alàbawö / a̱mù̱wö is used in your community?

chile.gloss: chili pepper (sweet; also generic hot chili per Chevrier)
chile.source: margery1996; constenla2010; chevrier2017 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'chile'; primary page not verified)
chile.note: Primary sources gloss dipa’ as 'chile dulce' (Capsicum spp.); Chevrier 2017 also lists it as generic 'chile picante'. Variant dapa’; also sha’. Card shows a red hot chili.
chile.reviewQuestion: Does dipa’ cover a hot red chili, or only sweet pepper? Is there a different word for the hot chili?

papa.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
papa.note: No Bribri entry for potato (Solanum tuberosum). Generic tu’ means 'tuber / yam' and would name a different food. No attested loan.
papa.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

aguacate.source: jara2018; chevrier2017 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'aguacate'; primary page not verified)
aguacate.reviewQuestion: Is ja̱mo̱’ or a̱mo̱’ the form used for avocado in your community?

tomate.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
tomate.note: No Bribri entry for tomato. No attested loan found.
tomate.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

girasol.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
girasol.note: No Bribri entry for sunflower. Generic 'flower' is attested (dakuà / mà̱ma̱) but would not identify this card. A phrase with dìwö 'sun' would be an invention, so not proposed.
girasol.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri name for the sunflower, or a Spanish loan in use? Would 'flower' (dakuà / mà̱ma̱) be acceptable?

sol.source: jaragarcia2013 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'sol'; primary page not verified)
sol.note: Everyday word. Sensitivity: the sun has mythological names (Dalàbulu, Dìwö Akë́köl) and a sun clan (Dìwöwak) — do NOT use those.
sol.reviewQuestion: Is dìwö correct for the sun picture?

luna.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2013; jaragarcia2003 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'luna'; primary page not verified)
luna.note: Variants si’wö and short si’ (Jara & García list si’ among the forms). Choose one per community.
luna.reviewQuestion: Which form do children use: síwö, si’wö or si’?

estrella.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'estrella'; primary page not verified)

lluvia.source: jara2018; margery1996; constenla1998 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'lluvia'; primary page not verified)
lluvia.note: Variant kò̱li̱ (dialectal a/o alternation in nasal syllables).
lluvia.reviewQuestion: Which variant is used in your community: kà̱li̱ or kò̱li̱?

rayo.source: garcia_com_pers (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'relámpago'; primary page not verified)
rayo.note: Single source: personal communication from Alí García Segura recorded in Krohn's dictionary. Thunder is alá. Sensitivity: thunder/lightning are tied to mythological beings (Kikílma̱, Télma̱, Talàchake, the thunder lords) — do NOT use those names; ritual-speech tkë́rme̱ also avoided.
rayo.reviewQuestion: Is talàwöñor the everyday word for a lightning bolt? Variant tlàwöñor?

arcoiris.source: margery1996 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'arcoíris'; primary page not verified)
arcoiris.note: Alternatives: tkabë̀ / tkabë̀köl (also 'snake'; Margery) and shkaba’ (Jara & García 2003, mythology dictionary). Sensitivity: in Bribri tradition the rainbow is associated with a serpent; dulà avoids the homonym with 'snake' (also a card). Do not confuse with Dulù (mythological serpent).
arcoiris.reviewQuestion: Which word do children use for the rainbow: dulà, tkabë̀köl or shkaba’? Is any of them sensitive?

nube.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'nube'; primary page not verified)

viento.source: jaragarcia2003; constenla1998 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'viento'; primary page not verified)
viento.note: Variants si̱wa̱’, su̱a̱’. Sensitivity: the same form also means 'knowledge' and 'sacred history / traditional narration' (Constenla et al. 1998; Jara & García 2003). Reviewer should confirm it is appropriate as a game word for 'wind'.
viento.reviewQuestion: Is su̱wa̱’ acceptable for the wind card given its other meaning ('sacred history')? Is there a better everyday word?

cometa.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
cometa.note: No Bribri entry for comet. Not inventing a descriptive phrase.
cometa.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri name for a comet (or 'star with a tail')? Or a Spanish loan in use?

montana.source: jaragarcia2013 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'montaña'; primary page not verified)
montana.reviewQuestion: Which variant is used in your community?

volcan.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
volcan.note: No Bribri entry for volcano (Talamanca has no active volcanoes). Not substituting 'mountain'.
volcan.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

manantial.source: margery1996; constenla2010 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'manantial'; primary page not verified)
manantial.note: Water spring / source. Appears in place names (e.g. Tùm Ajkö̀ Ki̱, Constenla 2010).
manantial.reviewQuestion: Is tù̱m the word for a water spring?

mar.source: margery1996; sanchez_sf (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'mar'; primary page not verified)
mar.note: Variants diyë̀, dyë̀. Sensitivity: ritual-speech words for the sea (Dulù, së̀) must NOT be used.
mar.reviewQuestion: Is dayë̀ right for the sea?

desierto.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
desierto.note: No Bribri entry for desert. Attested 'sand' (stsa̱’ña̱) or 'beach/sandy area' (tsà̱itö) would mean something else.
desierto.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

selva.source: jara2018; jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'selva'; primary page not verified)
selva.reviewQuestion: Is ka̱ñí̱k or kàlyök better for a rainforest picture?

cristal.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
cristal.note: No Bribri entry for crystal/quartz. SENSITIVITY: the sacred healing stones of Bribri healers (si̱a̱’, and ritual-speech names) are listed under 'piedra' and must NOT be used for a game card. Plain 'stone' ák exists but names a different thing. Wö̀sa̱wa̱k means 'mirror'.
cristal.reviewQuestion: Is there an everyday (non-sacred) word for a clear crystal or quartz? If the only words are sacred, should this card be skipped in Bribri?

isla.gloss: small river islet; also 'plot of land'
isla.source: margery1996 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'isla'; primary page not verified)
isla.note: Attested only for 'small island formed in a riverbed' (variants dara’, dra’, dta’). The card shows a sea island with palms, so this is a meaning mismatch. Note data’ also = 'dewlap' (Sánchez).
isla.reviewQuestion: Can data’ be used for an island in the sea, or is there another word?

cueva.source: constenla1998; margery1996; garcia_com_pers (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'cueva'; primary page not verified)
cueva.reviewQuestion: Is ká̱uk or úk used for a cave?

olla.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'olla'; primary page not verified)
olla.note: Differs from ù 'house' (card 'casa') only by nasality (macron below). Good teaching pair, but audio and spelling must keep them distinct; avoid using these two as each other's distractors without review.
olla.reviewQuestion: Is ù̱ used for a clay pot? Do children clearly distinguish ù̱ (pot) from ù (house)?

cesto.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2003; dipalicori_casa (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'canasta'; primary page not verified)
cesto.note: Variants jkö́, kö́. Also listed as 'ajkö / kö' in the DIPALICORI traditional house dictionary. Other basket word: àba 'canasto' (Margery). Avoid bika’, a ritual basket of healers.
cesto.reviewQuestion: Which is the everyday basket word: ajkö́ or àba?

tambor.source: margery1996; dipalicori_casa (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'tambor'; primary page not verified)
tambor.note: Variant sbák; synonym dulë̀ (Rimolo 2007; also 'traditional chicha-festival song' and 'small bird'). DIPALICORI house dictionary lists 'sabák/dulë'. Possible cultural note: drums accompany traditional dances/songs.
tambor.reviewQuestion: Is sabák the right word, and is there any ceremonial restriction on the drum?

adobe.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
adobe.note: No Bribri entry for adobe brick (not a traditional Bribri building material). dö́ means 'mud, clay' — a different thing.
adobe.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

hilo.source: margery1996; chevrier2017 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'hilo'; primary page not verified)
hilo.note: Means cord/thread/rope (synonyms stsa’, kichà); also the cabuya plant. Sensitivity: Ja̱mù̱ is also the name of a mythological being (owner of traps) per Jara & García 2003 — the common noun should be fine but confirm. Fine cotton thread: suítöm 'cotton cord' (Jara & García 2008).
hilo.reviewQuestion: Is ja̱mù̱ fine for sewing/weaving thread, or is suítöm better?

canoa.source: margery1996; krohn2016 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'canoa / bote'; primary page not verified)
canoa.note: Variants knò̱, ko̱nò̱. Krohn 2016 (lexical acculturation) also lists it; it may be a borrowing (cf. Spanish canoa). Kept as attested.
canoa.reviewQuestion: Is ka̱nò̱ a native word or felt to be a loan? Is it the everyday word?

puente.source: garcia_com_pers (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'puente'; primary page not verified)
puente.note: Single source (personal communication). Krohn's Spanish index lists shkë́k for 'puente', but its own Bribri entry for shkë́k means 'standing, upright' — conflicting; chose shkótkö, whose entry explicitly glosses 'puente'.
puente.reviewQuestion: What is the word for a bridge (hanging/rope bridge): shkótkö, shkë́k or another?

vela.source: constenla1998; margery1996 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'vela / candela'; primary page not verified)
vela.note: Constenla et al. 1998 gloss 'candela'; Margery 1996 'cera' (wax). Alternative akatùwö 'candela, vela' (Chevrier 2017).
vela.reviewQuestion: Which is used for a candle: bùlña̱ or akatùwö?

martillo.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
martillo.note: No Bribri entry for hammer. Verbs for hitting exist (tö́k, ppö́k) but no noun.
martillo.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

casa.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2013; dipalicori_casa (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'casa'; primary page not verified)
casa.note: Title word of the DIPALICORI traditional house dictionary. Combining form wé (as in compounds). Do not use chö́we / wéri (cultured/ritual speech). Minimal pair with ù̱ 'pot' (card 'olla').

milpa.source: constenla2010; jaragarcia2013 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'milpa'; primary page not verified)
milpa.note: Glossed 'sembradío, labranza, milpa'. A Bribri të̀ is a general cultivated plot, not specifically the Mesoamerican maize–bean–squash milpa.
milpa.reviewQuestion: Is të̀ the right word for a planted field?

tienda.source: constenla1998; krohn2016 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'tienda'; primary page not verified)
tienda.note: Compound with wé 'house'; dalì = 'cargo, goods'. Listed in Constenla et al. 1998 and in Krohn 2016 (lexical acculturation), i.e. a coined compound, not a loan.
tienda.reviewQuestion: Is dalì wé what people say for the local shop?

plaza.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
plaza.note: No Bribri entry for town square/plaza. ù apà / ùjkö mean 'house yard, patio' — not a public square.
plaza.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

puerto.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
puerto.reviewQuestion: Do children in your community use a Spanish loan for this (how is it pronounced/written in Bribri spelling), or is there a Bribri word or phrase?

pueblo.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
pueblo.note: No generic Bribri entry for village/town found; only place names and ká̱ kibí 'city' (Krohn 2016) and ká̱ 'place, land'. ká̱ kibí would name a city, not a village.
pueblo.reviewQuestion: What word or phrase is used for a village/community? Would ká̱ kibí be wrong here?

escuela.source: margery1996; jara2018 (as indexed in Krohn 2025 online dictionary, ES→BRI entry 'escuela'; primary page not verified)
escuela.note: Spelling varies: stsàwöwe (Margery), tsa’wöwe (Jara 2018), jtsàwöwe. Descriptive alternative se’ yawók wé 'house where we learn' (Krohn 2016). Compound with wé 'house'.
escuela.reviewQuestion: Which spelling/pronunciation is used locally: stsàwöwe, tsa’wöwe or jtsàwöwe?

observatorio.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
observatorio.note: No Bribri entry for observatory or telescope. Not coining a phrase.
observatorio.reviewQuestion: Is there a way to say 'observatory' (place to look at stars)? Otherwise skip this card in Bribri.

biblioteca.source: krohn2025 (no entry found under the Spanish lemma; also searched Bribri definitions)
biblioteca.note: No Bribri entry for library. Attested parts exist (uyë́jkuö 'book/paper'; X + wé 'house of X' as in dalì wé 'shop', stë̀ wé 'museum'), but no speaker-attested compound for 'library', so none is proposed.
biblioteca.reviewQuestion: Would uyë́jkuö wé ('book house') be natural for 'library', or is there an existing word?
